passage:
"Arnab! Arnab!" Kalyani, six, was on the floor by the stool, clutching her knee, blood on her fingers.
Arnab, her big brother, dropped his pencil and knelt. His stomach flipped, but he kept his voice slow. "Okay. I see it. Don't touch it."
"It hurts!"
"I know. You're being brave. Stay here, I'm getting Ma."
He walked quickly, not running, to the kitchen. "Ma, Kalyani fell off the stool. Her knee's bleeding. Not a lot."
Ma turned off the gas. "Where's the first-aid box?"
"Top of the cupboard. I'll bring it."
When Ma knelt by Kalyani, Arnab was already there with the box open and a bandage in his hand.
"You stayed so calm," Ma said.
"My heart didn't," Arnab admitted.

qa.q: Where was the first-aid box?
qa.a: On top of the cupboard.

qa.q: What did Arnab mean by "My heart didn't"?
qa.a: Arnab was frightened and sorry for Kalyani inside, but kept a steady voice and body so he could help.

qa.q: Which of Arnab's choices helped Kalyani most, and why?
qa.a: Telling Kalyani to stay put and going straight to Ma with clear facts brought an adult quickly, with the first-aid box ready.

qa.q: What might it be like for Kalyani to hear Arnab's slow voice?
qa.a: Kalyani, hurt and scared, would probably feel a bit calmer hearing her brother stay steady and promise that help was coming.

grounding: A boy sees his little sister fall, feels for her, and calmly fetches their mother and a bandage.

So I told Hafsa, 'Stay sitting, I'm getting Ma'am,' and ran to the staff room. Rao Ma'am came with the first-aid box and a bandage, and I held Hafsa's water bottle. Later Hafsa said I looked calm. I wasn't. I just knew what to do.

passage:
Thursday night
Today was the class trip to the botanical garden. On the rocky path near the lotus pond, Reena tripped and fell on her knee. It was bleeding a lot. Two girls screamed and one boy ran off.
My tummy went jumpy. I felt really sorry for her because her face was all crumpled. But I made my breathing slow, like we do in yoga, and said, "Reena, stay here. I'm getting Miss."
I walked fast, not ran, because the path was slippery. Miss D'Souza was near the bus. I told her, "Reena fell by the pond, her knee is bleeding." She grabbed the first-aid bag and I showed her the way.
Miss cleaned it, put on a big bandage and said, "Good boy, Joseph." Reena said thank you to me on the bus.
Joseph

qa.q: Where did Reena trip?
qa.a: On the rocky path near the lotus pond.

qa.q: What was Joseph feeling when he saw Reena's knee, and what did he do with that feeling?
qa.a: He felt jumpy and really sorry for her, but he slowed his breathing so the feeling stayed steady enough for him to go and get help.

qa.q: Which choice made the difference for Reena, and why?
qa.a: Joseph choosing to walk fast to Miss D'Souza and tell her exactly what happened mattered most, because it brought the first-aid bag and an adult quickly.

qa.q: How might Reena have felt when Joseph said he was getting Miss?
qa.a: She probably felt less alone and scared, knowing someone had a plan while the others screamed or ran off.

grounding: It shows a child who feels sorry when a classmate falls but keeps his body steady and fetches the teacher and a bandage instead of panicking.

passage:
Kabaddi had started on the mud ground behind the village school in Dhule when Pradeep slipped on a wet patch and landed hard on his wrist. He sat up holding it, face white, tears running.
The other boys crowded round, all shouting at once. One of them started crying too.
Siddharth, ten, felt his chest squeeze. Pradeep was his bench partner. But he didn't join the shouting. He took one long breath and said, "Don't move it. I'm calling Masterji."
He ran to the staff room, where Masterji was having tea, and said clearly, "Pradeep fell on his wrist. It's hurting badly." Masterji came with the red first-aid tin and a cloth for a sling.
Later, while Pradeep waited for his father, Siddharth sat beside him and shared his guava.

qa.q: What did Masterji bring?
qa.a: The red first-aid tin and a cloth for a sling.

qa.q: How can you tell Siddharth was upset even though he stayed calm?
qa.a: His chest squeezed when he saw Pradeep hurt, which shows he felt it strongly, but he chose to take a long breath instead of shouting.

qa.q: What went wrong in the crowd, and what did Siddharth do differently?
qa.a: The other boys shouted and one cried, which gave Pradeep no help; Siddharth stepped away from the noise and went straight to the one adult who could help.

qa.q: How might Masterji see Siddharth after this?
qa.a: Masterji might see him as a boy who can be trusted in an emergency, because he came clearly and quickly with the right information.

grounding: It shows a child who feels for a hurt friend but keeps a steady body and calmly fetches the teacher and first aid instead of joining the panic.
